fields.Question: What does 「〜ことができます」mean?
fields.Answer: To be able to do something / can do (expressing ability or potential).
fields.Marathi: मला जपानी बोलता येते — I can speak Japanese. Japanese dictionary form + ことができます and Marathi verb + ता येते share a beautiful parallel where the action is nominalized before expressing ability.
fields.Example:
Easy: 私は漢字を読むことができます (わたしは かんじを よむ ことができます) — I can read kanji. (Why: The dictionary form 読む is nominalized by ことができます to show reading ability.)
Medium: ここでカードで払うことができます (ここで カードで はらう ことができます) — You can pay by card here. (Why: Expresses situational possibility of payment using the verb 払う.)
Hard: 私は日本語で簡単な手紙を書くことができます (わたしは にほんごで かんたんな てがみを かく ことができます) — I can write a simple letter in Japanese. (Why: Combines multiple modifiers like "in Japanese" and "simple letter" with the dictionary form verb "書く" to express capability.)
fields.Mnemonic:
こと turns a verb into "the act of [verb]-ing" (like English "-ing" as a noun), and できます means
"is possible" — so literally "the act of doing X is possible." Picture turning the verb into a
noun-shaped object before handing it to できます.
fields.AI Notes:
Common mistake: attaching ことができます to the ます-form instead of the plain dictionary form (❌
食べますことができます, ✅ 食べることができます). Also don't confuse this with the shorter potential-verb
form (食べられます) — N5 typically expects ことができます first; the direct potential form is more N4.

fields.Question: What does 「い-adjective (affirmative)」mean?
fields.Answer: Expresses a present or future affirmative state or quality using an adjective ending in "い" in its polite form.
fields.Marathi: हा चहा खूप गरम आहे। — This tea is very hot. Both languages share the SOV sentence structure where the adjective precedes the closing polite state marker (です / आहे).
fields.Example:
Easy: 今日は寒いです。(きょうはさむいです) — Today is cold. (Why: The "い" adjective 寒い ends in "いです" for polite present affirmation.)
Medium: この本はとても面白いです。(このほんはとてもおもしろいです) — This book is very interesting. (Why: The adverb とても modifies the "い" adjective to add emphasis.)
Hard: わたしの部屋は狭いですが、きれいです。(わたしのへやはせまいですが、きれいです) — My room is small, but it is clean. (Why: Links an "い" adjective clause using が to show contrast before a "な" adjective predicate.)
fields.Mnemonic:
い-adjectives already end in い — no extra copula needed to "make" them an adjective, just add です
for politeness (寒い → 寒いです).
fields.AI Notes:
Common mistake: adding な after an い-adjective when modifying a noun (❌ 寒いな日) — な is only for
な-adjectives; い-adjectives attach directly to the noun (寒い日).

fields.Question: What does 「い-adjective negative (~くないです)」mean?
fields.Answer: Expresses a present or future negative state or quality for an "い" adjective by dropping "い" and adding "くないです".
fields.Marathi: हा रस्ता चांगला नाही। — This road is not good. Both languages show a parallel where the affirmative adjective is modified at its end to express negation before the final verb/copula.
fields.Example:
Easy: 今日は寒くないです。(きょうはさむくないです) — Today is not cold. (Why: The "い" of 寒い is dropped and replaced with くないです to conjugate to negative.)
Medium: その辞書はあまり良くないです。(そのじしょはあまりよくないです) — That dictionary is not very good. (Why: The irregular adjective いい changes to よ before adding くないです, modified by the negative-favouring adverb あまり.)
Hard: このアパートの家賃は安くないですが、便利です。(このあぱーとのやちんはやすくないですが、べんりです) — The rent of this apartment is not cheap, but it is convenient. (Why: Shows a negative "い" adjective contrasting clause linked to a positive "な" adjective.)
fields.Mnemonic: Drop the final い, add くない — "i" leaves, "ku-nai" arrives.
fields.AI Notes:
Common mistake: forgetting いい (good) is irregular — its negative is よくない, not いくない. Memorize
いい/よい as the one standout exception among い-adjectives.

fields.Medium: 四月は春です。(April is spring.)
fields.Hard: 四月になりますから、新しい学校が始まります。(April comes, so the new school starts.)

fields.Medium: 金曜日は楽しみです。(I look forward to Friday.)
fields.Hard: 金曜日ですから、今晩友達と食事します。(It's Friday, so I'll eat with a friend tonight.)
